about: Idea cards for the invention lab. Each seat is dealt three, from three different families, and answers its framings with them. A card is a forcing move: it pushes the seat away from the feature anyone would add. The TRIZ principles are applied to the thing itself; the separation principles resolve one of its contradictions; SCAMPER moves change one of its parts; the material cards start from what the thing already has; the morphology cards use the frame's box; the far fields are places to borrow a solution from; the time cards move the thing in time.

cards.name: Segmentation
cards.prompt: Split one part of the thing into pieces a person could use, move or share on their own.

cards.name: Taking out
cards.prompt: Take the one part people value most out of the thing, and let it live on its own somewhere else.

cards.name: Local quality
cards.prompt: Make one part behave differently for each person, place, moment or device, instead of the same for everyone.

cards.name: Dynamics
cards.prompt: Let something fixed in the thing change by itself as the person or the situation changes.

cards.name: Prior action
cards.prompt: Do part of the person's work before they ask, so it is ready the moment they arrive.

cards.name: Nesting
cards.prompt: Put the thing, or a piece of it, inside another thing people already use every day.

cards.name: Universality
cards.prompt: Make one part do two jobs at once, so another part is no longer needed.

cards.name: Feedback
cards.prompt: Show people, as they go, the effect of what they just did, or what others did before them.

cards.name: Self-service
cards.prompt: Let the thing serve, repair, explain or improve itself, using what it already does.

cards.name: Turn harm into benefit
cards.prompt: Take what annoys people most about the thing (a wait, an error, a limit) and make it the feature.

cards.name: The other way round
cards.prompt: Invert one flow: the thing comes to the person, the end comes first, the user teaches the tool.

cards.name: Partial or excessive action
cards.prompt: When doing it exactly right is hard, do far more or far less of it, and see what that opens.

cards.name: Another dimension
cards.prompt: Move one part to another level: from one person to a group, from a screen to the room, from a page to a place.

cards.name: Cheap short-lived copies
cards.prompt: Replace something lasting and costly in the thing with many quick, disposable versions.

cards.name: Separate in time
cards.prompt: Let both sides of the contradiction hold, at different moments of using the thing.

cards.name: Separate in space
cards.prompt: Let both sides hold in different places: different screens, devices, modes or people.

cards.name: Separate on condition
cards.prompt: Let each side hold only when a condition is met: for some people, some tasks, some sizes.

cards.name: Separate the part from the whole
cards.prompt: Let the whole have one property and its parts the opposite: simple as a whole, deep in each part.

cards.name: Substitute
cards.prompt: Replace one part of the thing with something from a different material: voice for text, a gesture for a form, a picture for a list.

cards.name: Combine
cards.prompt: Join two parts of the thing that never meet today into one new part.

cards.name: Adapt
cards.prompt: Take something that works in another thing these people use, and fit it to this one.

cards.name: Magnify
cards.prompt: Take the smallest detail of the thing and make it the centre of it.

cards.name: Put to another use
cards.prompt: Use the thing, or what it makes, for a job it was never meant for.

cards.name: Eliminate
cards.prompt: Remove the step, screen or part everyone assumes is needed, and invent what replaces it.

cards.name: Rearrange
cards.prompt: Change the order: what comes last comes first, what is hidden is shown, what is shown is hidden.

cards.name: What it knows
cards.prompt: Start from something the thing knows or collects (its D… items) and invent what that knowledge could do for the person.

cards.name: The unused capability
cards.prompt: Start from something its platform could do and it does not (its U… items), and invent the thing that needs exactly that.

cards.name: The by-product
cards.prompt: The thing leaves traces: drafts, logs, half-finished journeys, searches with no result. Make one of them valuable.

cards.name: The idle moment
cards.prompt: Find the moment when the person waits, hesitates or leaves, and invent what belongs there.

cards.name: The second person
cards.prompt: Someone else touches the thing too (a helper, an admin, a viewer, a buyer's boss). Invent something for them.

cards.name: What leaves it
cards.prompt: Something leaves the thing (an export, a link, a printout, a message). Make what leaves it do more than it does.

cards.name: The weak spot
cards.prompt: Start from one of its weak spots or workarounds (its W… items): invent the thing that makes the workaround unnecessary.

cards.name: An empty cell
cards.prompt: In the morphological box, pick a combination of options nothing of this kind has, and describe the thing that would have it.

cards.name: One dimension to the extreme
cards.prompt: Take one dimension of the box and move the thing to the option furthest from where it is today.

cards.name: Two far options together
cards.prompt: Join the two options of two dimensions that seem least likely to go together.

cards.name: How nature does it
cards.prompt: An organism solves this problem (finding, signalling, remembering, adapting, repairing): borrow its mechanism.

cards.name: How a game does it
cards.prompt: Levels, quests, saves, discovery, play with others: borrow one mechanic that would change how people use the thing.

cards.name: How a craftsman's tool does it
cards.prompt: A good tool fits the hand, wears in, and shows its use: borrow one quality of a well-made tool.

cards.name: How a kitchen does it
cards.prompt: Preparation before service, stations, a pass, tasting as you go: borrow one way a kitchen works.

cards.name: How a city does it
cards.prompt: Signs, districts, transit lines, landmarks, public squares: borrow one way a city helps strangers find their way.

cards.name: How a museum does it
cards.prompt: Curation, a guided route, the one object in the room, the label you read up close: borrow one.

cards.name: How a coach does it
cards.prompt: Watching a person practise, the one correction at a time, the plan for next week: borrow one.

cards.name: How a musical instrument does it
cards.prompt: Played, not operated: tuned, practised, expressive, the same for a beginner and a master. Borrow one quality.

cards.name: Before it is needed
cards.prompt: What could the thing do for the person before they know they need it?

cards.name: After it is done
cards.prompt: What could the thing do for the person after the job they came for is finished?

cards.name: In one second
cards.prompt: What would the thing be if its main job had to take one second?

cards.name: Over a year
cards.prompt: What would the thing be if it remembered and grew with the same person over a whole year?

cards.name: Ten years on
cards.prompt: What will things of this kind do in ten years that this one could start doing now?
